Explanation: The selectable unit is a live travel offer: a priced flight, stay, rental car or package from a travel supplier or booking intermediary that the traveler can compare and then choose where to book.
KAYAK Software Corporation operates the metasearch interface and is part of Booking Holdings. KAYAK organizes travel offers and referrals but does not own the underlying travel products.
KAYAK must turn fragmented prices and availability from many sellers into one useful comparison for a specific trip.
KAYAK earns from referrals and advertising. Providers can pay when travelers click through or complete bookings, while sponsored placements create additional advertising revenue.
KAYAK depends on accurate, current prices and on traveler trust. Rapid price and availability changes can create mismatches between a displayed offer and the provider site.
KAYAK captures travel intent, compares offers and then hands the traveler to the selected Travel Provider for the actual booking relationship.
Transaction Flows: ← Consumer · Search Intent — Travelers send destination, route, dates, budget and other trip criteria into KAYAK. | → Consumer · Compare Offers — KAYAK returns ranked, filterable travel offers from multiple sellers so the traveler can decide where to book. | ← Provider · Direct Rates — Airlines, hotels and other direct suppliers contribute prices, availability and booking routes to KAYAK. | → Provider · Direct Clicks — When a traveler chooses a direct option, KAYAK sends qualified referral traffic to the travel supplier. | ← Partner · OTA Rates — Online travel agencies contribute alternative seller offers for the same or comparable travel products. | → Partner · OTA Clicks — When the traveler chooses an OTA offer, KAYAK sends the referral to that booking platform, which then owns the booking and payment relationship.

Explanation: KAYAK sets result-ordering rules, labels sponsored placements and provider identity, and applies pricing, legal and service standards to booking partners.
KAYAK attracts high-intent demand through its brand, search visibility, apps, price alerts, travel tools and other marketing channels.
Core activities are collecting live offers, normalizing data, matching trip intent, ranking results, maintaining price tools and routing referrals.
KAYAK’s key resources are traveler search intent, broad price and availability feeds, comparison technology, brand trust and historical search data.
Consumers are leisure and business travelers comparing flights, stays, rental cars or packages before deciding where to book.
Travelers want to find an option that fits their dates, route, budget and preferences without checking many travel sites manually.
KAYAK can expose multiple sellers for the same travel product, making prices and booking conditions easier to compare in one place.
Travelers face changing prices, many similar options, different fees and conditions, and uncertainty about which seller will handle the booking.
Travelers submit trip criteria, compare results and select a provider or booking site to continue toward purchase.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Search Intent — Travelers send destination, route, dates, budget and other trip criteria into KAYAK. | ← Owner · Compare Offers — KAYAK returns ranked, filterable travel offers from multiple sellers so the traveler can decide where to book.

Explanation: Travelers filter by dates, route, destination, price, timing, stops, property attributes, provider and other trip preferences.
Travelers use KAYAK’s websites and apps, along with search tools such as price alerts and Explore, to access the comparison layer.
Travelers search, sort, filter and compare before choosing which seller should receive the booking click.
Travelers contribute destination or route, travel dates, party needs, budget, preferences and attention to the comparison process.
Providers are direct travel suppliers such as airlines, hotels and car-rental companies. They control the underlying travel product and can appear as direct booking options in KAYAK results.
Direct suppliers want high-intent travelers to choose their own offer and complete the reservation with them rather than through another intermediary.
KAYAK sends travelers who have already expressed specific dates, routes and product preferences, making referral traffic highly relevant to the supplier.
Suppliers may pay for clicks or bookings and must keep prices competitive and accurately synchronized across KAYAK and other distribution channels.
Suppliers provide prices and availability; KAYAK can return qualified referral traffic when a traveler chooses the direct option.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Direct Rates — Airlines, hotels and other direct suppliers contribute prices, availability and booking routes to KAYAK. | ← Owner · Direct Clicks — When a traveler chooses a direct option, KAYAK sends qualified referral traffic to the travel supplier.

Explanation: Travel companies shown by KAYAK must meet pricing, legal and service standards and supply sufficiently usable pricing and availability data.
Direct suppliers connect through commercial integrations, price and availability feeds, referral links and other provider connections.
Suppliers set prices and availability, accept the booking, collect payment when applicable and deliver the actual travel service.
They contribute the underlying seats, rooms or vehicles together with live prices, schedules, availability, rules and checkout capability.

Online travel agencies such as Expedia, Booking.com and other booking sites act as intermediary sellers. They can offer the same underlying travel product alongside a direct supplier, creating a platform-to-platform comparison layer.
OTAs aggregate travel supply, package it into their own booking experience and compete for KAYAK’s high-intent referral traffic.
KAYAK can send OTAs travelers who are already comparing a specific trip and are close to choosing a seller.
OTAs must compete on price, service and conversion while paying for qualified referrals and maintaining accurate offer data.
OTAs contribute bookable offers and can pay KAYAK when a traveler clicks through or completes a booking under the commercial arrangement.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · OTA Rates — Online travel agencies contribute alternative seller offers for the same or comparable travel products. | ← Owner · OTA Clicks — When the traveler chooses an OTA offer, KAYAK sends the referral to that booking platform, which then owns the booking and payment relationship.

Explanation: KAYAK says booking companies must meet pricing, legal and service standards and are reviewed regularly for compliance.
OTAs connect their offers and booking destinations to KAYAK through commercial data feeds and referral integrations.
OTAs aggregate supplier inventory, price and package offers, run checkout and provide booking confirmation and customer service.
They contribute aggregated inventory, pricing, booking technology, payment capability and post-booking servicing.
